response.sql: SELECT player_id, SUM(triple) AS total_triple FROM batting_postseason WHERE player_id IN (SELECT player_id FROM batting_postseason WHERE league_id = 'NL' INTERSECT SELECT player_id FROM batting_postseason WHERE round = 'WS') GROUP BY player_id ORDER BY total_triple DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A player qualifies if they have at least one postseason batting record with league_id = 'NL' and at least one with round = 'WS', and those two records may be different rows. The total then sums triple across all of that player's postseason batting records.
'NL' is matched on batting_postseason.league_id = 'NL' and 'World Series' is matched on round = 'WS', which is the Lahman coding for the World Series.
SUM ignores NULL triple values, and a player whose triples are all NULL gets a NULL total, which NULLS LAST places at the bottom. Ties in total_triple are ordered arbitrarily.

alternatives.interpretation: The NL and World Series conditions must hold on the same postseason batting record (league_id = 'NL' AND round = 'WS'). Qualifying players are those with at least one such record, and their total triples still sum across all of their postseason records.
alternatives.sql: SELECT player_id, SUM(triple) AS total_triple FROM batting_postseason WHERE player_id IN (SELECT player_id FROM batting_postseason WHERE league_id = 'NL' AND round = 'WS') GROUP BY player_id ORDER BY total_triple DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
